structural_progress.claim: every declared task has at least one feasible typed worker/resource path; tasks absent from must_reachable_tasks remain outcome-conditional

assumptions: The reserve initially contains 50 items and has capacity 100; no task outside this contract changes it.
At the time origin there are no preexisting active invocations or undelivered handoffs; all later work is counted by these activation envelopes.
For each producer, admitted invocation counts in every interval of t milliseconds lie between max(0, (t-100)/100) and 1+t/100 for all time.
Consumer admissions reserve one item immediately; counts in every interval lie between max(0, (t-50)/50) and 1+t/50 for all time.
Each worker has one dedicated, work-conserving slot providing t worker-milliseconds in every backlogged interval of length t; no unmodeled competing work or blocking reduces that availability.
timing:produce-first/duration, timing:produce-second/duration, and timing:consume/duration are assumed upper bounds of 9 ms each.
timing:produce-first/dispatch, timing:produce-second/dispatch, and timing:consume/dispatch are assumed wait upper bounds of 1 ms each.
Every producer completion adds exactly one item, every consumer admission removes exactly one item, and no overflow discard or failure path changes those declared effects.
claims.statement: Conditional on the declared all-time arrival and service envelopes, the two producing workers keep the reserve at least 30 percent full for all t >= 0, while the admitted flow stays within its 100-item capacity.

metadata.purpose: Explicit conditional reserve promise, with measurements unnecessary for assumed envelopes.
Two independent producing workers maintain a shared reserve above thirty percent capacity.
